public_rationale: Goldman's April 15, 2026 report describes one unnamed industry datapoint in which engineering inference costs were approaching 10% of engineering headcount cost [e1]. This supports the approximate spending component as a reported anecdote, but the report supplies no matched evidence about that company's stability, quality or efficiency gains [e1]. It therefore does not settle the combined claim that such spending occurred without demonstrated gains [e1].
limitations: The company, underlying spending accounts, compensation denominator and accounting period are undisclosed.
The figure concerns engineering headcount costs, not all employee costs, and says 'approaching' 10%.
Silence about operational benefits does not establish their absence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Some companies spend up to 10% of employee costs on generative AI without apparent stability, quality or efficiency gains.

statement.excerpt: To simplify, this means that some companies are spending as much as 10% of the cost of their employees on generative AI services, all without appearing to provide any stability, quality or efficiency gains, or (not that I want this) justification to lay people off.

from_speaker: as much as 10% of the cost of their employees
without appearing to provide any stability, quality or efficiency gains
our_interpretation: Read 'some companies' existentially: at least one qualifying company would suffice.
The immediately preceding Goldman passage concerns engineering headcount costs, so use that denominator rather than all company employees.
Read 'without appearing' as absence of demonstrated gains at the qualifying company, not a universal claim that AI never helps.
Use April 2026, the contemporaneous reporting month identified by 'last week', as the observation window. The underlying spending accounting period is unspecified.
The spending ratio and operational outcomes must concern the same company and period.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence identifies a company spending approximately 10% of engineering headcount cost on generative AI and establishes no demonstrated stability, quality or efficiency gains in that setting.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence disproves the cited spending ratio or shows demonstrated gains at the same company underlying the anecdote. Gains at unrelated companies do not refute an existential claim.
